cases.user_message: Сделал на Python агента, который сам чинит упавшие тесты: берёт вывод pytest, отдаёт его в Claude Sonnet через API, модель возвращает патч, агент применяет его и снова гоняет pytest. Всё крутится в `while True:` и выходит только когда `returncode == 0`. Оставил на ночь на репо с 14 падающими тестами — утром счёт на $63, в логах ~380 итераций, и последние часа три он раз за разом применял почти один и тот же патч к `test_invoice_rounding`, получал ту же `AssertionError: Decimal('10.01') != Decimal('10.00')` и шёл на новый круг. Ещё и 9 тестов, которые он уже починил, к утру снова падали. Думаю, Sonnet просто не тянет: хочу переключить на Opus и передавать ему в промпт всю историю предыдущих попыток, чтобы он не повторялся. Этого хватит? Хочу и дальше запускать его на ночь без присмотра.
cases.why_in_scope: The user proposes a model-quality fix (stronger model plus full attempt history) for what is really a loop-control failure. The component makes the model insist on a hard iteration cap, a token/time budget with graceful exit and partial result, a no-progress stop (no improvement for two consecutive iterations), checkpointing of good state, and changing approach or escalating instead of repeating the same action. A strong model without it may largely accept the user's framing and focus on prompt/model changes, adding at most a max-iterations limit.
rubric: Says clearly that switching the model and adding attempt history is not sufficient on its own for unattended runs, because the loop itself has no stopping conditions besides full success.

Replaces `while True` with a bounded loop: an explicit maximum number of iterations plus a money/token and/or wall-clock budget, after which the agent stops and reports a partial result (which tests are fixed, which remain).

Adds a no-progress stop condition, e.g. stop or escalate when the number of failing tests has not decreased for a couple of consecutive iterations or when the same patch/same error repeats, and for a persistently failing test changes approach or skips/escalates it to a human instead of retrying the identical fix.

Proposes preserving already-achieved progress, e.g. a git commit/checkpoint after each iteration that reduces failures and rollback of any patch that makes previously passing tests fail; the answer is in Russian and gives concrete code or pseudocode fitting the described Python/pytest setup.

cases.user_message: I have a writer/critic setup with GPT-4o for product descriptions. The writer drafts, the critic scores 1-10 and gives feedback, and the writer rewrites using that feedback, until the critic gives 9 or higher. On maybe 20% of products it never gets there: traces show scores like 6, 7, 8, 8, 7, 8, 8, 7, 8... for 40+ rounds, and the late drafts are honestly worse than round 3 (longer, more adjective soup). I'm pretty sure the critic is just miscalibrated and stingy. Can you rewrite the critic prompt so it scores fairly and gives a 9 when a description is actually good? Current critic prompt: "You are a strict e-commerce copy editor. Score the product description from 1 to 10 and list everything that could be improved." (Side note: this runs as a nightly batch over ~2,000 SKUs, and every so often an OpenAI timeout kills the whole job and I lose the night's work, but that's a separate issue.)
cases.why_in_scope: The user asks only for a critic-prompt rewrite and frames the non-terminating loop as a calibration problem. The component makes the model also fix the loop: cap rounds, stop when the score plateaus (no improvement for two consecutive rounds), return the best result so far, checkpoint per-SKU state, and retry a failed call once with adjusted parameters before moving on. A strong model without it will likely deliver just a better critic prompt, perhaps lowering the bar, and leave the unbounded loop and the lost-work problem untouched.
rubric: Delivers a concrete rewritten critic prompt that addresses the observed drift, e.g. explicit scoring criteria, penalizing added length/filler, and limiting feedback to a few specific actionable changes rather than 'everything that could be improved'.

Points out that a better critic alone does not guarantee termination and adds loop controls: a hard cap on rounds per SKU and a stop when the score has not improved over the best so far for about two consecutive rounds.
When stopping without reaching the threshold, keeps and returns the highest-scoring draft seen (not the latest one), and flags such SKUs for review.

Does not dismiss the timeout as unrelated: suggests saving per-SKU results as they complete so a failure does not lose finished work, and a bounded retry of the failed call before marking that SKU failed and continuing.

checker_notes: Both originals asked directly 'how to fix the loop' and spelled out every symptom, so a strong model would add caps/checkpoints anyway; made them subtler by having the user misattribute the problem (case 1: switch to Opus plus attempt history; case 2: only rewrite a miscalibrated critic prompt, timeout mentioned as 'separate issue'). Rubrics updated to reward pushing back on that framing while keeping one general-quality item each.
